statement: Always name the product "Quillmark Pulse".
Use "team members" when writing about our people.
do_example: Our team members in Bengaluru build it.

statement: dashboard is lowercase when generic; "Insights dashboard" is not a product.
Product names must match current approved naming; "Quillmark Insights" was renamed to "Quillmark Pulse" in June 2026.
Company name is "Quillmark Analytics"; short form "Quillmark" allowed after first mention.
Every statistic in public content must trace to a fact in the Fact Library.
Superlatives ("#1", "best", "India's leading") need an approved source behind them.
do_example: An analytics platform trusted by 2,300+ teams.

statement: Customer counts may only use the Fact Library figure for active customer teams.
Write percentages and prices exactly as approved: up to two decimals, INR as 1,299/month.
Certifications (ISO, SOC 2) may only be claimed while the certificate is current.
Keep sentences short on average: aim under 20 words per sentence.
dont_example: We are pleased to announce a comprehensive suite of capabilities that spans the entire governance lifecycle of your organisation's brand content estate and further.

statement: Tone is "confident, never pushy"; no hard-sell phrases.
do_example: Meet Quillmark Pulse. Analytics your team can trust.
dont_example: Just 999/month! Grab it NOW before it's gone!!

statement: Address the reader as "you".
do_example: You can fix claims in one click.

statement: At most ONE exclamation mark per post, and never in a claim sentence.
Lead with approved messaging pillars: easier decisions
column8: Data-driven synergy for the digital age.

statement: Never name competitors negatively or by implication.
Sales posts end with a clear call to action.
dont_example: Great content though we forgot what to do next.

statement: Promotional claims must be substantiated as required by CCPA Guidelines on Misleading Advertisements (2022).
do_example: Claim with citation to approved fact.

statement: A disclaimer cannot fix a misleading headline claim (CCPA guidance).
Prices in INR with rupee formatting as approved in the Fact Library.
Content citing regulations earns explicit legal review before approval.
Images in posts need descriptive alt text.
do_example: Screenshot with alt text "Dashboard view showing revenue trend".
dont_example: Empty alt attribute on the screenshot.

statement: Keep reading level at or below grade 10 for public content.
dont_example: Long sentences with jargon and dense clauses.

statement: Do not convey meaning with colour alone.
do_example: Highlight and label the failing row.
dont_example: Highlight failing row in red only.

statement: Blog posts use section headings (H2) and a summary line.
Marketing emails include an unsubscribe link.
do_example: Powered by Quillmark; unsubscribe any time.
dont_example: No opt-out anywhere in the email.

statement: One-pagers place the locked-up logo top-left with clear space.
Content referencing certifications must show current certificate status from the Fact Library.
dont_example: ISO claim with no validity check.

statement: Publishing goes through review; nobody posts approved content outside the approved window.
Use the approved palette: Ink #101828
Logo is never stretched
do_example: recoloured or placed over busy backgrounds.

statement: Tagline is exactly "Every claim checked against the truth you approved.".
do_example: Every claim checked against the truth you approved.
dont_example: Every claim checked with AI magic.

statement: Personal data in content follows DPDP Act 2023 principles; no personal screenshots with visible names.
Confidential figures never appear in public content.
do_example: Public content uses approved public facts.

statement: Social posts under 200 words with a first-line hook.
Hashtags: max 3 per post
Web pages show live pricing from the Fact Library and a valid-to date.
Agency drafts carry a client-rule checklist before submission.
Template fields (price
do_example: customer count) are filled only from the Fact Library.

statement: Be bold but friendly.
Keep it fresh and also strictly formal traditional at all times.
Use current product names at all times.
Make it engaging.
